verses.1: And in the third year of Hoshea son of Elah, king of Israel, reigned Hizkia son of Ahaz, king of Judah.
verses.2: He ruled for forty-five years. He also ruled in Jerusalem for forty-nine years. His mother’s name was Abi Bat Zekhariyah.
verses.3: And he did what was right in the eyes of Jehovah, just as his father David had done.
verses.4: He removed the idols and broke the idols. He also destroyed those who were worshiping them. Moses was called “Nunhushtan” because until those days, the Israelites still worshipped those idols.
verses.5: In the LORD, the God of Israel, he had confidence. After him, none else could compare to him among all the kings of Judah who came before him.
verses.6: And he kept away from anything that was not in accordance with Jehovah’s commands. He obeyed the laws that Jehovah had given Moses.
verses.7: And Jehovah will be with him in all that he does. He will rebel against the king of Assyria, and he will not serve him.
verses.8: He conquered the Philistines all the way to Gaza, and his territory extended from the hill of Nobim to the city of Mibzor.
verses.9: And it was in the fourth year of King Hizkiah’s reign that Shalmaneser, king of Assyria, rose up against Shinar. He created a siege wall around it.
verses.10: And she was captured from the age of three years old, in the year six of Hezekiah’s reign. It was the year forty during the reign of King Israel’s king. She was captured by Shmuel.
verses.11: And King Ashur led Israel out of Assyria. He settled them in the valleys and along the banks of the river Gozan, as well as in the cities of Madi.
verses.12: For they did not hear the voice of the LORD their God, and they broke the covenant that Moses commanded them to keep. They did not listen, nor did they carry out those commands.
verses.13: And in the forty-fifth year of King Hizkiah, Sanherib, king of Assyria, invaded all the cities of Judah.
verses.14: And Hizkiah, king of Judah, sent a message to King Ashur. He said, “I have sinned again. I will take up fire on myself.” So King Ashur imposed a tax of three talents of silver and thirty talents of gold on Hizkiah, king of Judah.
verses.15: And Hizkia gave away all the money that was found in the Temple of God and in the treasures of the King’s palace.
verses.16: On that day, Hizkiah sealed the doors of the Temple of Yahweh, as well as all the treasures that Hizkiah had planned to keep. He gave these treasures to King Ashur.
verses.17: And the king of Assyria sent Tarshan, Rehob’s son, and Rehabeam from Lakish to the king of Judah, Hizkiah. They brought with them a glorious army from Jerusalem. They went up and arrived in Jerusalem. They stood on the bank of the river Kishon.
verses.18: And they called out to the king. Eliaqim son of Hilkiah, who was in charge of the building, and Yoah son of Asaf the scribe, came out to them.
verses.19: And Rab-shakhe said to them, “Please speak to Hizkiah about this.” This is what the great king, King Ashur, said: What is this assurance that you have given?
verses.20: You said only what is right and wise for war. Now, against whom do you hope to win? For you have rebelled against Me.
verses.21: Now, now you have been assured of this promise regarding the acquisition of this desirable land for Egypt. It will be given to anyone who possesses it, and it will be taken from him. Thus, Pharaoh, the king of Egypt, will give this land to all those who are worthy of it.
verses.22: And when they said to me, “To the LORD our God,” we trusted that He would indeed remove Hazekiah from his throne and from all his idols. Then He said to Judah and Jerusalem, “In front of this altar, you shall worship in Jerusalem.”
verses.23: And now, please go ahead and meet with King Ashur. I will give you one thousand horses, if you can manage to ride them.
verses.24: And how can you restore the face of one of Adonai’s little servants? And how can you ensure that Egypt will be able to ride on that chariot and be freed from its captivity?
verses.25: Now, I, the servant of the LORD, have come to this place in order to destroy it. The LORD said to me, “Go and destroy this land.”
verses.26: And he said to Eljakim, son of Hilkiah, and to Shebna and Yoah: “Speak to your servants in Aramaic. For we can hear, but do not speak to us in Hebrew in the ears of the people who are present here.”
verses.27: And he said to them, “Rab Shakhah, let me speak to you about these matters. They concern those who sit around the fire, eating their food and drinking from their feet.”
verses.28: And Rab-shakhe stood up and cried out in a loud voice, in Hebrew. He spoke and said, “Hear the words of the great king, King Ashur.”
verses.29: So said the king, “Al-Yashia will give you strength. For he cannot save you by his own hands.”
verses.30: And let Khizkiah not trust you in the hands of Jehovah, saying, “Yahweh will save us.” Do not give this city into the hands of King Ashur.
verses.31: Do not listen to Hizkiah. For this is what the king of Assyria said: “I will bless you, and you shall come to me. Then you shall eat the flesh of your gods and drink the blood of your idols.”
verses.32: Until then, I will take you to the land that is like your own land. It will be a land of grains and fruits; a land with vineyards, figs, and herbs. You shall live there forever, and you shall not die. And do not listen to Hizkiah, for he will try to deceive you by saying, “The LORD will save us.”
verses.33: The savior saved them from the king of Assyria’s hands. The gods of the nations saved each person from their land.
verses.34: Oh God of fire and destruction! Oh God of chaos and destruction! How can You save Shemeron from their hands?
verses.35: Who among all the gods of the earth has ever saved his land from my hands? For Jehovah will save Jerusalem from my hands as well.
verses.36: And the people refused to obey him. They did not respond to his commands, because it was the king’s command: “Do not obey him.”
verses.37: And he went to Eliakim, son of Hilkiya, who was in the house. There, the scribe and Yoah, son of Asaf, told him about the events that had happened to Hizkia. They recounted to him what had taken place.
